change.author: nicktrn

findings.title: A backup code plus any dummy totpCode logs in without the password
findings.body: The password is only checked when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new backup-code branch (line 131) runs whenever `backupCode` is set, and it never looks at `totpCode`. Anyone can POST straight to the credentials callback with `email`, `totpCode: "x"` and one valid `backupCode`. That skips the password check (line 121), takes the backup-code branch, and returns the user at lines 205-214. A leaked backup code (for example the downloaded `cal-backup-codes.txt`) is then enough to sign in, with no password. A backup code should replace only the second factor. Fix: always verify the password in the backup-code branch, for example by rejecting the request when `credentials.totpCode` is also set or by calling `verifyPassword` inside the branch. Separately, the existing rule that a `totpCode` skips the password check is worth a look, since it makes TOTP alone sufficient.

findings.title: Using up a backup code is not atomic
findings.body: The codes are read when the user is fetched (line 89), checked in memory, and then written back with a plain update (lines 149-156). Two login requests sent at the same moment with the same code will both pass `indexOf` before either write lands, so a code meant for one use can open two sessions. A conditional update (`where: { id, backupCodes: <old ciphertext> }`, failing if no row matches) or a transaction would enforce single use.

findings.title: Closing the backup-codes step with Escape or an outside click leaves the settings page saying 2FA is off
findings.body: The enable call now only moves to `DisplayBackupCodes` (line 135). `onEnable`, which runs `utils.viewer.me.invalidate()` in `apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:65-68`, is only called from the Close button (line 269). If the user dismisses the dialog with Escape or an outside click, `onOpenChange` (two-factor-auth.tsx:64) just sets `open` to false. 2FA is now on at the server, but the cached `me` data still says off, so the switch and badge are wrong and nothing tells the user. `step` also stays at `DisplayBackupCodes`, so clicking the switch reopens this modal on the codes screen. Fix: call `onEnable()`/`resetState()` from `onOpenChange` once the step is `DisplayBackupCodes`, or block dismissal on that step.

findings.title: The "copied" toast shows even when the clipboard write fails
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` returns a promise. It is not awaited, and `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` runs right away. If the write is rejected (permission denied, document not focused), the user is still told the codes were copied, may close the dialog trusting that, and is then left without their recovery codes. Fix: await the promise, show the success toast only once it resolves, and show an error toast when it rejects.

findings.title: `missing_backup_codes` tells users to generate codes in settings, but there is no screen for that
findings.body: Codes are only created by `setup.ts` while 2FA is being enabled (setup.ts:61-71), and setup refuses once 2FA is on (setup.ts:42-44). Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have `backupCodes = NULL`, so they see this message, and no settings screen can generate codes. The only route is to disable 2FA and enable it again. The text should say that, or the PR should add a way to regenerate codes.

findings.title: `tabIndex={-1}` makes the show/hide-password toggle unreachable by keyboard everywhere
findings.body: `PasswordField` is shared, so this change hits every password input in the app: login, signup, the security settings and both 2FA modals. Keyboard-only users can no longer reach the visibility toggle. If the aim was only to stop the toggle from sitting in the tab order on the login form, consider making it opt-in through a prop.

findings.title: The BackupCode component is exported as `TwoFactor`
findings.body: The default export is named `TwoFactor`, the same name as the component in `TwoFactor.tsx`. Both are imported side by side in `login.tsx` and `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, so stack traces and React DevTools will show two components with the same name. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

findings.title: Submitting an empty backup code shows no error
findings.body: The login form has `noValidate` (line 188), so the `required`/`minLength` attributes on the BackupCode input are never enforced. With `backupCode` empty, `authorize` falls through to the TOTP branch and throws `SecondFactorRequired`. `onSubmit` handles that by calling `setTwoFactorRequired(true)` (line 156), which is already true, so the user sees nothing. Add a client-side check, or show an error for that code while `twoFactorLostAccess` is set.

findings.title: No test covers logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The new tests only click the download, copy and close buttons. Logging in with a backup code, refusing a code that was already used, and disabling 2FA with a backup code all go untested, and these are the security-relevant paths (see the password-bypass finding). Adding at least a test that logs in with a code and then fails to reuse it would protect them.

contracts.action: Log in with a backup code instead of a TOTP code
contracts.before_after: Both branches run after the password check at lines 121-129, which is skipped whenever totpCode is set. The TOTP branch at least verifies the TOTP it was given. The backup branch verifies only the backup code, so a dummy totpCode lets a request skip both the password and the TOTP.
contracts.visible_effect: A session is created (login.tsx:155 router.push). Error codes are mapped at login.tsx:157-158.
contracts.failure_mode: A wrong code throws IncorrectBackupCode and the user sees 'Backup code is incorrect.'. Missing codes throw MissingBackupCodes. A missing encryption key throws InternalServerError.

contracts.action: Enable 2FA, then show the backup codes before calling onEnable
contracts.equivalent_path: Before this PR, onEnable was called right after the enable succeeded
contracts.before_after: onEnable (setEnableModalOpen(false) plus a me.invalidate) now runs only from the Close button. Dismissing through onOpenChange does neither.
contracts.visible_effect: The settings switch reflects the me query (two-factor-auth.tsx:48), which goes stale if the dialog is dismissed without Close.
contracts.failure_mode: Escape or an outside click leaves 2FA enabled at the server while the UI shows it off, and the step stays at DisplayBackupCodes for the next open.

contracts.action: Download the backup codes from a Button inside an <a download> inside the TOTP Form
contracts.equivalent_path: The Close and Copy buttons, which call preventDefault
contracts.before_after: Button defaults to type="button", so clicking Download does not submit the enclosing Form. The anchor's default download action runs.
contracts.visible_effect: The browser downloads cal-backup-codes.txt, which the e2e test asserts.

contracts.before_after: For CAL users the password is checked first (lines 40-45) in both branches. Afterwards both clear backupCodes, twoFactorEnabled and twoFactorSecret.
contracts.visible_effect: The modal calls onDisable, which invalidates the me query. Errors are mapped at DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:67-79.
contracts.failure_mode: Wrong or missing codes return 400 with the matching error code. A missing key throws, as the existing branch already does.

summary: The PR adds 2FA backup codes. Generation, storage, display and their use for disabling 2FA all look right, apart from a few problems below. The blocker is in `next-auth-options.ts`. The backup-code branch never checks `totpCode`, and the password check is skipped whenever `totpCode` is set. So a request with a dummy `totpCode` and one valid backup code logs in without the password. There are two fix-level problems in the enable modal. First, dismissing the backup-codes step with Escape or an outside click leaves the settings page showing 2FA as off, even though it is on. Second, the "copied" toast shows even when the clipboard write fails. Also flagged as consider: single use of a code is not enforced against concurrent requests, a locale message points to a settings screen that does not exist, the password-visibility toggle is now unreachable by keyboard in every `PasswordField`, `BackupCode` is exported under the name `TwoFactor`, an empty backup code fails with no error, and no tests cover backup-code login or disable.
